newsitem.title: USA: Atmel to pursue Silicon lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Atmel to pursue Silicon lawsuit.

text.p: Atmel Corp said Thursday it would press ahead with a lawsuit that claims Silicon Storage Technology Inc (SST) is infringing on five of its patents.

Atmel, a designer and manufacturer of flash memory components, said it was encouraged a preliminary ruling by U.S. District Court Judge Samuel Conti, even though he denied the company's motion for a summary judgment in the case.
Atmel, based in San Jose, said the judge's June 25 ruling reduced the amount of evidence it would have to present at the trial, which is scheduled to begin on November 24.
The opinion involved Atmel's motion for the court to rule at once that SST infringed on two of the five patents.

"Although Atmel did not get all the relief it requested in these motions, these rulings greatly reduce the amount of evidence that Atmel will have to present at trial in order to prove SST's infringement of these two patents...," Atmel Chief Financial Officer Kris Chellam said in a statement.
But Silicon Storage's chief executive, Bing Yeh, told Reuters in an interview that his company viewed the ruling as favorable and remained confident it would prevail in court.

"The court basically raised serious questions about that claim, and we still remain confident we will win at the trial," he said, drawing attention to SST's counterclaim that it has complied with longstanding industry standards.

The case involves technologies used in flash memories, used to store data in small handheld and portable computers. SST, based in Sunnyvale, Calif., designs medium-density flash memories for Taiwanese PC makers.

Atmel's '903 patent involves technology used to identify memory chips so computer programs can recognize specific devices, and its '811 patent involves high-voltage computer circuit technology. Silicon Storage argues the first patent is a widely adopted standard and that its products differ from the '811 patent.

In his ruling, the judge found Silicon Storage infringed on four of the six contested claim elements concerning Atmel's '811 patent and one of two contested claim elements concerning the '903 patent, Atmel said.
SST's Yeh said there are no discussions under way on settling the case.

In a related development, Atmel said an International Trade Commission law judge on June 12 denied a Silicon Storage motion to make a summary determination that Silicon Storage did not infringe on the '903 patent.

Atmel had requested that the ITC investigate whether Sanyo Electric Co Ltd, Winbond Electronics Corp and Macronix Inc were engaged in unfair practices by importing products into the United States that Atmel claims infringe on its patents.
Atmel said Silicon Storage had intervened in that action because Sanyo and Winbond produce products for SST.
The outcome of the lawsuit in federal court is expected to influence the course of the ITC investigation.
